This study selected the central urban area of Wuhan as the study area, where extensive urban development coexists with diverse ecological spaces. items.titel: From cemeteries to ecological memorial landscapes: the rise of green and conservation burial grounds and its opportunities for urban planning
items.samenvatting_bron: The article conducts an interpretative review of contemporary scientific literature (2000–2026) to analyse the environmental aspects of conventional funeral practices and introduces sustainable burial cemetery models such as green cemetery and conservation burial grounds. The interdisciplinary literature review covers landscape architecture, urban planning, urban ecology, environmental sciences, and sustainable development research. The ecological memorial landscapes, which promote human biomass “return” back into biological cycles, could create ecosystems that merge into urban green infrastructure networks, and transform the end-of-life into an active mechanism for environmental preservation. City planners and landscape architects are uniquely positioned to promote this sustainable model by reimagining and zoning cemeteries as urban green infrastructure. This study suggests that despite legal, religious, and cultural barriers, the rise of eco burial practices signals a generational evolution and shift toward ecological accountability and “death positivity” movement.

items.samenvatting_bron: Introduction Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) contains highly diverse aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems but remains underrepresented in biodiversity research. Methods A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 was conducted using Google Scholar and Scopus for studies published from January 2018 to April 2026. Eligible peer-reviewed English-language studies used eDNA or DNA metabarcoding to assess aquatic or terrestrial biodiversity in SSA. items.titel: Contribution of eDNA Metabarcoding to Model Ecosystems: Case Study of Threatened Peri-Urban Mediterranean River
items.samenvatting_bron: Freshwater ecosystems on Mediterranean islands are threatened refuges where conventional bioassessments often fail to capture the full spectrum of biotic assemblages. Here, environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding targeting the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene was applied across three representative sampling reaches (Upstream, Midstream, Downstream) of the Oreto River (Sicily, Italy) during a single sampling campaign to assess vertebrate composition. This targeted spatial snapshot captured aquatic, semi-aquatic, and terrestrial signals. items.titel: Marine Mammal Monitoring Research from 2014 to 2023: A Bibliometric Analysis of Collaboration, Technological Trends and Research Themes
items.samenvatting_bron: Marine mammal monitoring research has expanded considerably alongside developments in acoustic, remote-sensing, telemetry, molecular, and computational approaches. This study used bibliometric analysis to characterise the structure and evolution of research published between 2014 and 2023. A total of 2586 peer-reviewed publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection were analysed using CiteSpace to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, temporal clusters, and citation bursts. Annual publication output increased from 155 articles in 2014 to a peak of 362 in 2022, while collaboration networks revealed prominent research hubs across North America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania. Passive acoustic monitoring remained a persistent and highly connected theme, alongside habitat modelling, environmental impact assessment, and conservation research. Temporal and keyword analyses indicated increasing attention to machine learning, artificial intelligence, remote sensing, and environmental DNA, reflecting a broader movement towards automated and multimodal monitoring approaches. Existing research on urban NBS barriers focuses mostly on structural and technical elements, while co-creation and local knowledge are regularly cited as critical for successful implementation. Even when barriers are easy to identify, a divide between ambition and reality generates procedural and knowledge gaps. This paper addresses this challenge through a case study of the Horizon Europe project URBREATH. Narrative inquiry is used to reveal invisible aspects of NBS implementation as experienced by city officials from Madrid, Cluj-Napoca, Leuven, and Tallinn. items.titel: Spatiotemporal Evolution and Driving Forces of Green Spaces in Shrinking Cities
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban shrinkage causes inefficient land utilization and landscape fragmentation. Green spaces are critical nature-based solutions for the sustainable development of shrinking cities, and play an important role in enhancing urban environmental quality and promoting residents’ physical and mental well-being. Using landscape ecological indices (PLAND, NP, and LPI) coupled with the spatial Durbin model (SDM), geographically weighted regression (GWR) and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR), this study investigates the dynamics and influencing factors of green space in shrinking cities from 2000 to 2020. The results show that cities with population shrinkage experience the concurrent expansion and fragmentation of green spaces, cities with economic shrinkage demonstrate modest changes accompanied by low fragmentation, and cities with social shrinkage face a decline in green spaces with reduced patch numbers. The dynamics of green space are driven by the interplay of socioeconomic and natural factors, where the former operate at broader spatial scales and the latter exert localized influences. Consequently, spatial governance of urban green spaces should be implemented through multidimensional and multi-scalar coordinated strategies.
